title: Mysterious Tiles Have Been Appearing In City Streets Since The 1980s
description:
Since the early 1980s, cryptic tiles have been embedded into the asphalt of major city streets. Nobody has ever been officially credited with making them.

Coverage of the 2011 documentary Resurrect Dead and its investigation into Severino Verna

scenes.text: Since the early 1980s, strange tiles have been turning up embedded in the asphalt of city streets, from Philadelphia all the way to Chile.
They're about license plate sized, made of layered linoleum, and nearly impossible to remove once they've fused into the road.
Almost all of them carry the same message: Toynbee idea in movie 2001, resurrect dead on planet Jupiter.
Some later tiles added something stranger, and darker, phrases like 'murder every journalist, I beg of you,' with no explanation attached.
In 2011, a documentary crew spent years tracing the tiles to a reclusive Philadelphia man, Severino Verna, after finding his home address on one of the tiles, found in Chile.
He never confirmed it publicly, and nobody has ever been officially credited. New tiles are still turning up decades later, and nobody knows who's still making them.
